audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags it directly: Malphite wins 54.65% over 1409 games, but the level chart hands Jax 5 of 7 stages and Malphite none. The content prose disagrees with its own chart — spikes[3] calls 2+ items 'your reclaim window' and whys[6] says 'you reclaim the duel', yet win[6] is set to Jax.
audit.why: The lane genuinely is Jax's from level 2 to first item: Counter Strike at 17s rank 1 plus Empower burst beats a Malphite with no armour yet. But the 2+ item stage is where armour scaling makes Ground Slam hurt and the attack-speed cripple guts an auto-reliant duellist, which is precisely why the overall win rate is above 50%.
audit.corrected: 2+ items should read Malphite, matching the prose already on the page. I could not propose the flip as an edit — see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate is called 'Grandmaster's Might' in four places across the content layer. That is the old name.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon gives the ability as Grandmaster-at-Arms, 110/100/90s. The described effect — bonus Armor and Magic Resist plus a magic-damage proc on every third consecutive attack — is accurate, so only the name is wrong.
audit.corrected: Name corrected to Grandmaster-at-Arms in spikes[2], wants.foe[2], mid and whys[4]; the 110s cooldown added so the level-6 spike has a clock.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says Counter Strike 'dodges your W Thunderclap autos and stuns you' — correct as far as it goes — but never states the half that tells you what to DO, and it appears nowhere in either layer.
audit.why: Riot's text: Counter Strike lets Jax 'dodge all incoming attacks'. Attacks, not abilities. Ground Slam and Seismic Shard land through an active Counter Strike untouched, and Ground Slam is the ability that cripples the attack speed his whole kit runs on. So the correct play during his E is to stop auto-attacking and press E — the page currently implies you should simply back off. Second missing piece: Empower is a 7/6/5/4/3s auto-attack RESET, so the burst tell is the wind-up, not the cast. Third: Unstoppable Force dashes with displacement immunity, so Counter Strike's stun cannot deter it once airborne — it only beats the cast.
audit.corrected: Both layers now say abilities land through Counter Strike, name Empower's reset as the burst tell, and state that R is not deterred once airborne.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Track Counter Strike' appears in nine places with no cooldown attached.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9s — at rank 1 that is a 17-second hole, the longest punishable window in the lane. Leap Strike at 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s is his gap-closer and Empower is only 7s falling to 3s, so Counter Strike is the only cooldown worth planning a commit around.
audit.corrected: The 17s number added as the commit clock.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization carries the unfilled template parenthetical '(by his AD profile)' and offers 'Thornmail / Abyssal Mask' as if the choice were arbitrary.
audit.why: Jax is mostly physical, so armour and Plated Steelcaps are correct, but Grandmaster-at-Arms adds magic damage on every third attack and grants him MR, which is the actual reason a splash of MR later is not wasted. Frozen Heart is the standout here because its attack-speed reduction stacks with Ground Slam's cripple against a champion who lives on attack speed.
audit.corrected: Armour core kept and Frozen Heart called out for the attack-speed stacking reason.

audit.why: Beyond the ultimate's name, the content layer's mechanical claims check out against the kit: Granite Shield buffering level-1 autos, Counter Strike dodging empowered autos, and Ground Slam's attack-speed reduction gutting an auto-reliant duellist are all supported.

edits.after: Counter Strike dodges attacks, not abilities — Ground Slam still lands, it just barely hurts before you own any armor.

edits.before: Granite Shield actually gives you a real level-1 here — it eats his opening autos, so contest the wave instead of conceding it. But once Jax has E Counter Strike at level 3, do not trade into him: his E dodges your W Thunderclap autos and stuns you, and you have no armor yet to make Ground Slam hurt. Throw Q Seismic Shard to chip and slow him so he cannot freely reset onto you, last-hit safe, and let your shield refresh between his pokes.
edits.after: Granite Shield actually gives you a real level-1 here — it eats his opening autos, so contest the wave instead of conceding it. But once Jax has Counter Strike at level 3, stop auto-attacking into it: it dodges attacks, so your Thunderclap autos whiff and you get stunned. It does NOT dodge abilities — Ground Slam and Seismic Shard land through it, they just barely hurt with no armor yet. Chip with Q, last-hit safe, and let the shield refresh between his pokes.

edits.before: This is his window, not yours. At 6 his R Grandmaster's Might stacks resistances and adds the on-hit magic proc, so a straight all-in favors him until you have armor items. Use Q to kite and deny him free E-stun trades, hold E Ground Slam to shred his attack speed the moment he commits autos, and only fight back when Granite Shield is up. If he dives, your R Unstoppable Force is your escape and counter-engage — bait the E stun first, then knock him up.
edits.after: This is his window, not yours. At 6 his R Grandmaster-at-Arms stacks resistances and adds a magic proc every third attack, so a straight all-in favors him until you have armor items. The rule during his E: never auto, always ability — Counter Strike dodges attacks and nothing else, so Ground Slam lands and cripples the attack speed his kit runs on. His Empower is a 7s auto reset, so the wind-up is the tell. If he dives, R counter-engages: it dashes displacement-immune.

notes: LEVEL-CHART CONTRADICTION (packet-flagged, unresolved): the chart gives Jax 5 of 7 stages and Malphite 0 despite a 54.65% Malphite win rate over 1409 games, and win[6] says Jax while the very same file's spikes[3] calls 2+ items 'your reclaim window' and whys[6] says 'you reclaim the duel'. The correct value is Malphite for 2+ items. I did not propose the edit because 'Jax' to 'Malphite' is a 3-to-8 character change and the applier's length band rejects anything past 10% — this needs either a hand fix or an applier exemption for side/win enum fields. Same structural issue blocked the Irelia level-6 flip. Jax's ultimate is Grandmaster-at-Arms in Riot Data Dragon; the content layer used the retired name 'Grandmaster's Might' in four places. R displacement immunity web-verified on League Wiki ('the dash cannot be deterred by crowd control').
